findings.problem: JobWorkflow has no state machine enum; status is a free-form String and lifecycle flags are separate booleans, so any combination of status/bools is representable including impossible ones like status="sent" with is_validated=false
findings.failure_mode: invalid state combinations (e.g. sent-but-not-validated, unsent-but-is_sent=true) propagate through the system without detection, breaking downstream invariants
findings.fix: replace status/is_validated/is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms with a single JobState enum with variants that encode the lifecycle transitions and owned data, e.g. enum JobState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }

findings.problem: status is declared as pub status: String, allowing any arbitrary string value; mark_sent sets it to a hardcoded literal string rather than a typed transition
findings.failure_mode: callers can set status to any string (e.g. "sent", "SENT", "", "pending", "deleted"), making pattern matching on workflow state impossible and breaking all state-dependent logic
findings.fix: replace String with a domain enum JobStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and use match/arm-based transitions

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are separate lifecycle booleans that can exist in contradictory combinations (e.g. is_sent=true but status!="sent", is_validated=false with is_sent=true)
findings.failure_mode: lifecycle state is distributed across independent booleans with no ordering constraint; callers can construct contradictory states and there is no single source of truth for workflow lifecycle
findings.fix: collapse is_validated and is_sent into a single enum typestate where each variant represents a valid lifecycle stage; move sent_at_epoch_ms into the variant that owns it

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is a bare Option<u64> separate from the lifecycle flags; it can be Some(_) even when is_sent=false and status is not "sent", and None when is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: optional lifecycle data is decoupled from the lifecycle flags, allowing timestamps on non-sent jobs and missing timestamps on sent jobs, violating domain invariants
findings.fix: move sent_at_epoch_ms into the enum variant that owns the sent lifecycle stage, e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }, making it impossible to have a timestamp without the sent state

findings.problem: id is declared as pub id: String, a raw primitive with no domain constraints; any string including empty or malformed identifiers is accepted
findings.failure_mode: illegal identifier states (empty string, whitespace-only, non-unique) are indistinguishable from valid IDs at the type level, leading to potential duplicate or missing job lookups
findings.fix: wrap in a newtype: pub struct JobId(String) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty input, or use a crate like ulid/uuid

findings.problem: raw String primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct JobWorkflow with any string for id and status, and any bool combination, so invalid domain states are directly creatable
findings.failure_mode: no parsing or validation layer exists at the struct boundary; every caller bypasses domain rules by directly constructing JobWorkflow fields with untrusted primitives
findings.fix: replace raw fields with domain types (newtype JobId, enum JobState) and provide a single fallible constructor fn try_new(id: &str, ...) -> Result<JobWorkflow, JobError> that parses and validates at the boundary

no profiler data to confirm mark_sent is a hot path
no allocation evidence showing mark_sent heap allocates on every call (status.to_string() allocates)
no second-ring evidence for any claimed performance characteristics
no command-truth evidence (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test) was run or reported
residual_risk: review is source-only static analysis; no commands were executed. The code has zero typestate enforcement, six independent fields allowing arbitrary invalid state combinations, and a raw String parse boundary. Even without benchmarks, the structural violations are sufficient to block delivery under Holzman absolute laws.
